Implement the storage half of work package G in the callisto repo (Rust workspace): `crates/callisto-model/src/format/pre.rs` must read and write both Changesets v2 and v3 `pre.json` shapes. Touch only `pre.rs` (plus its tests and the minimal call-site edits in other crates that are needed to compile). Do not change aggregation, release-decision allowed paths, or ADRs; the parent session does that later.

Background (verified):
- v2 shape: `{ "mode": "pre"|"exit", "tag": "...", "initialVersions": {name: version}, "changesets": [ids] }`. That is all callisto parses today (`parse_pre_json`, `render_pre_json`, `write_pre_json_preserving`).
- v3 shape (Changesets v3): only `{ "mode", "tag" }`. `initialVersions` and the `changesets` id list are gone; consumed prerelease notes move to `.changeset/pre/*.md` instead. Today callisto fails v3 with E114 missing `initialVersions`.
- Settled decision: written back in the shape it was read. No silent migration.
- Unknown extra keys must not be dropped on a rewrite (callisto currently drops them); preserve them in original order.

What to build:
- `pub enum PreStateShape { V2, V3 }` determined from the file on read (v3 = neither `initialVersions` nor `changesets` present; exactly one of the two present is a malformed file: keep a clear error). Carry it on `PreState` (or a wrapper) so writers emit the shape read. `PreState::entering` keeps producing V2 (new cycles callisto starts stay v2 for now) unless trivially parameterisable.
- For V3, `initial_versions` is absent: model that honestly (e.g. `Option`, or an enum payload) rather than an empty map that silently means "no baseline"; follow the type-first rule below. Then fix callers so they compile and behave sensibly: where a caller needs a baseline version and the state is V3, fall back to what it already falls back to when a package is missing from `initialVersions` (grep `pre_initial_version` and `initial_versions` across crates). Keep caller edits minimal and list each in your report.
- `changesets` id list likewise absent in V3 (retained notes are identified by living in `.changeset/pre/`, which the parent handles). Model it so V3 has no id list; do not invent one.
- Preserve unknown keys and BOM/CRLF/indent fingerprint on rewrite (existing `write_pre_json_preserving`).
- Tests (in the existing test module style of the file): v3 parse; v3 round-trip writes `{mode, tag}` only; v2 round-trip unchanged; unknown keys preserved; half-v3 file rejected; `exiting()` on V3 writes v3.

Repo rules (from AGENTS.md, binding): safe Rust; no `unwrap()` outside tests (`expect` names the invariant); user-facing errors derive `miette::Diagnostic` with code and help; enforce invariants with types/exhaustive matches before tests; no source-scanning tests; one-line comments only for non-obvious why; no emojis.

Build budget: export `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=$(( $(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN) / 4 ))`. Iterate with `cargo test -p callisto-model` and `cargo clippy -p callisto-model --all-targets -- -D warnings`, then `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo test -p callisto-graph -p callisto-cli` for affected callers. Run cargo commands unsandboxed if the sandbox blocks them. Never run two cargo builds at once. Judge by exit code.

When done: commit on your worktree branch with a signed commit (never disable signing), conventional message `feat(model): read and write Changesets v3 pre.json`, no session links. Do not push. Report: branch name, worktree path, commit sha, the public API you added (signatures), each caller you changed and why, and the exact commands you ran with their exit codes.
